item.title: U.S. Embassy urges Americans to leave Lebanon over Iran university threats
item.description:
The U.S. Embassy in Beirut issued an urgent security alert on Friday urging all American citizens to depart Lebanon while commercial flights remain available, warning that Iran and its allied militias "may intend to target universities in Lebanon."

The advisory described the security environment as "volatile and unpredictable," citing ongoing airstrikes, drone activity, and rocket fire across the country, particularly in southern Lebanon, the Beqaa region, and parts of Beirut. "Iran has specifically threatened American universities across the Middle East," the embassy said, though it did not identify any specific institutions at risk.

item.title: Min Aung Hlaing wins parliamentary vote to become Myanmar president
item.description:
Myanmar's former military chief Min Aung Hlaing was elected president on Friday by the country's junta-installed parliament, completing a transition five years in the making from coup leader to nominal civilian head of state. The 69-year-old general, who seized power in 2021 by ousting the democratically elected government of Nobel Peace Prize laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, won the presidency in a bicameral vote that was widely seen as a foregone conclusion, with pro-military lawmakers controlling roughly 86 percent of parliamentary seats.

The vote, held at 10:00 a.m. local time in the capital Naypyidaw, saw members of both legislative chambers choose from among three vice-presidential candidates: Min Aung Hlaing, Nan Ni Ni Aye of the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party, and former Prime Minister U Nyo Saw, a retired lieutenant general and close Min Aung Hlaing ally. Union Parliament Speaker U Aung Lin Dwe had confirmed on Thursday that all three candidates met the constitutional qualifications for the presidency.

item.title: Asia fuel crisis deepens as Songkran, Easter travel face sweeping flight cuts
item.description: A cascading jet fuel crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israel military strikes on Iran on February 28 is upending travel plans across two continents as the Easter holiday weekend and Southeast Asia's Songkran New Year celebrations approach, with airlines slashing routes, raising fares, and warning of further disruptions ahead.

item.title: Debris from intercepted drones hits buildings across Dubai
item.description: Debris from an intercepted Iranian drone struck the facade of Oracle's building in Dubai Internet City early Saturday, as the Gulf conflict entered its fifth week with no sign of abating. The Dubai Media Office confirmed the incident in a post on X, calling it a "minor incident" and saying no injuries were reported.

item.title: Iran's Khamenei has 'no role in leadership' due to severe injuries, report says
item.description:
More than a month after Israeli fighter jets struck the supreme leader's compound in Tehran, Iran's new leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not been seen in public, and a hospital source has told The Media Line that he remains in a medical intensive care unit at an underground location with devastating injuries including a nonfunctional arm, paralyzed leg, spinal cord damage, and brain trauma.

The detailed account, published by The Media Line on Thursday, represents the most comprehensive report yet on the 56-year-old cleric's condition since the February 28 strike that killed his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, along with Mojtaba's wife, son, and several senior military officials.

item.title: Artemis II crew now closer to moon than Earth
item.description:
NASA on Friday unveiled the first photographs taken by the Artemis II crew, showing Earth in vivid detail as the four astronauts voyage toward the moon on the first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years.

The images, captured by mission commander Reid Wiseman through a window of the Orion spacecraft, show Earth's blue oceans draped in swirling white clouds, with green auroras shimmering at the poles. One photograph, titled "Hello, World," depicts the Atlantic Ocean bordered by a thin halo of atmosphere as Earth casts a shadow on the sun. Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen said the crew was "glued to the window" as they watched their home planet shrink behind them.

item.title: Five EU finance ministers demand windfall tax on energy firms
item.description:
Finance ministers from Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Austria are jointly calling on the European Commission to impose a windfall profit tax on energy companies benefiting from surging fuel prices driven by the war in Iran, according to a letter obtained by Reuters on Saturday.

The letter, dated Friday, argued that such a measure would signal that "we stand united and are able to take action," and would send "a clear message that those who profit from the consequences of the war must do their part to ease the burden on the general public," the ministers wrote.

item.title: NATO chief Rutte to meet Trump amid US exit threats
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte will travel to Washington next week for a face-to-face meeting with President Donald Trump on Wednesday, April 8, as the transatlantic alliance faces its most serious internal crisis in decades. The visit comes days after Trump told Reuters he was "absolutely without question" considering withdrawing the United States from NATO, citing European allies' refusal to support the U.S.-Israeli military campaign in Iran.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strikes kill one in Taganrog, hit chemical plants deep in Russia
item.description:
A wave of Ukrainian drone and missile attacks struck southern Russia early Saturday, killing at least one person and seriously wounding four others in the port city of Taganrog, while a separate drone raid targeted chemical plants deep inside Russian territory in the city of Tolyatti.

Rostov region governor Yuri Slyusar said the attack on Taganrog left one dead and four in critical condition, including a foreign citizen. Commercial infrastructure was damaged and a fire broke out at the warehouses of a logistics company, he wrote on Telegram.

item.title: Global chip sales surge 61.8% in February to $88.8B
item.description: The global semiconductor industry posted its strongest monthly growth in years, with worldwide chip sales climbing 61.8% year-over-year in February to reach $88.8 billion, the Semiconductor Industry Association reported on April 3, 2026. Sales also rose 7.6% from the January 2026 total of $82.5 billion, underscoring accelerating momentum in a sector fueled by insatiable demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Russia kills at least 15 in massive drone, missile barrage across Ukraine
item.description: Russian forces unleashed a wave of missile and drone strikes across Ukraine on Friday and into Saturday, killing at least 15 people and wounding dozens more in what officials described as part of an escalating pattern of daytime aerial assaults designed to maximize civilian harm.

item.title: Nations crack down on youth social media as bans spread globally
item.description: A wave of legislative and regulatory action is sweeping across multiple continents as governments move to restrict minors' access to social media, emboldened by landmark jury verdicts that found Meta and Google liable for harming children through their platforms.

item.title: Meta halts work with AI startup Mercor after data breach
item.description: Meta has suspended all collaboration with AI training startup Mercor while investigating a data breach that may have exposed sensitive AI industry information, according to a report from Wired on Friday and confirmed by a person familiar with the matter to Business Insider. The pause has left thousands of contractors unable to log hours on Meta-related AI training projects.

item.title: Israeli forces attack Gaza on 177th day of ceasefire
item.description: Israeli forces carried out fresh attacks across multiple areas of the Gaza Strip on Saturday, marking what Palestinian authorities described as the 177th consecutive day of violations since a U.S.-brokered ceasefire took effect on October 11, 2025.

item.title: U.S. F-15E shot down over Iran as IDF strikes Tehran
item.description: The Israeli Air Force launched what it called an "extensive" wave of airstrikes against Iranian military infrastructure in Tehran on Friday, April 3, as the five-week-old U.S.-Israeli war against Iran continued to escalate amid the loss of an American fighter jet over Iranian territory the same day.

item.title: Iran hits Kuwait refinery, UAE gas hub as war enters sixth week
item.description: Iran continued its sweeping retaliatory campaign across the Middle East on Friday and Saturday, hitting Kuwait's largest oil refinery, damaging energy infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates, and launching ballistic missiles at central Israel as the conflict triggered by the U.S.-Israeli offensive of February 28 showed no signs of abating.

item.title: Zelenskyy arrives in Istanbul for talks with Erdogan
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Istanbul on Saturday for talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, as Kyiv presses ahead with diplomatic efforts ahead of Orthodox Easter and amid a stalled peace process with Russia. Zelenskyy is also set to meet Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, the spiritual leader of Orthodox Christianity, underscoring the religious and cultural dimensions of the visit.

item.title: Israel strikes Beirut after destroying bridges over Lebanon's Litani River
item.description: Israel launched fresh airstrikes on Beirut early Saturday and destroyed a bridge in eastern Lebanon, escalating a month-old war against Hezbollah that has killed more than 1,300 people across the country.

item.title: Polymarket bets on $120 oil jump after Iran strikes Gulf
item.description:
Oil prices surged to their highest levels since 2022 this week after Iran launched a fresh wave of strikes on Gulf energy infrastructure, sending prediction market bettors scrambling to price in the possibility of even steeper gains. On Polymarket, the implied probability that WTI crude will touch $120 per barrel at some point in April has climbed to 77%, according to the platform's live market data, up from 65% just days earlier.

The repricing followed a dramatic escalation on Friday, April 3, when Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery — which has a capacity of 346,000 barrels per day — setting off fires across the facility. Kuwait also reported an Iranian attack that caused material damage to a power and water desalination plant. Separately, Abu Dhabi suspended operations at its largest natural gas processing facility after debris from a projectile interception sparked a fire, and Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted several drones.

item.title: Turkey confirms second ship crosses Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
A second Turkish-flagged ship has crossed the Strait of Hormuz, Turkey's Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu confirmed on Saturday, even as a fleet of Omani tankers charted a new route through the contested waterway that bypasses Iran's controlled corridor entirely.

The developments mark a cautious expansion of traffic through the strait, which has seen a roughly 95 percent drop in daily vessel movements since the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the conflict on February 28. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps imposed a selective blockade around March 14, routing permitted ships through a checkpoint between the Iranian islands of Larak and Qeshm.
